title: Per-customer amortization and SLO premium — quick math
content:
Purpose: capture quick heuristics for per-customer unit economics when we need to offer Dedicated/Private contracts + an SLO premium. This is intentionally rough — meant for convo with SEs and GTM when sizing asks.

Context + goal:
- We want a simple, explainable way to quote: 1) baseline per-active-user cost for hosted inference; 2) an amortized per-MAU for reserved/Dedicated capacity; 3) a percent premium for tighter SLOs / latency-sensitive routes.
- Keep two outputs: a) back-of-envelope per-MAU hosted cost (to derive PAYG floor), b) per-MAU amortized cost when customer signs a reserved capacity tranche.

Assumptions (plausible ballpark numbers for quick calc):
- Avg tokens per interaction (prompt+response): 750 tokens (interactive assistant with short context).
- Avg requests per active user per month: 120 (about 4/day).
- Model mix (by volume): 60% small (3B), 30% medium (13B), 10% large (70B).
- GPU-hour cost (amortized infra + power + k8s + telemetry): $3.00 per GPU-hour (hosted spot-equivalent bucket baseline).
- Throughput tokens/sec (rough): 3B -> 150 tps, 13B -> 50 tps, 70B -> 20 tps.
- Operational overhead (networking, storage, KMS, telemetry): +30% on top of token compute cost.
- Target gross margin target for hosted price: 20% (for simple sticker math).

Derive per-token compute cost (very rough):
- tokens/hr = tps * 3600.
  - 3B: 150 * 3600 = 540k tokens/hr => per-token = $3 / 540k = $0.00000556
  - 13B: 50 * 3600 = 180k tokens/hr => per-token = $3 / 180k = $0.00001667
  - 70B: 20 * 3600 = 72k tokens/hr => per-token = $3 / 72k = $0.00004167

Per-request compute cost (750 tokens):
- 3B: 750 * 0.00000556 = $0.00417
- 13B: 750 * 0.00001667 = $0.01250 (approx $0.0128 earlier; using 0.01667 here)
- 70B: 750 * 0.00004167 = $0.03125

Weighted average request cost (model mix):
- weighted = 0.6*0.00417 + 0.3*0.0125 + 0.1*0.03125 = 0.0025 + 0.00375 + 0.003125 = $0.009375 per request (compute only)
- Monthly per-MAU compute cost = 120 * $0.009375 = $1.125 per MAU/month
- Add operational overhead (+30%): $1.125 * 1.3 = $1.4625
- Add target margin 20% => price floor = $1.4625 / 0.8 = $1.828 per MAU/month (rounded ~$1.83)

Takeaway 1 (hosted PAYG floor for this persona): ~$1.8 per MAU/month to cover compute+ops+20% margin given these assumptions.

Reserved / Dedicated amortization sketch:
- Example: customer needs steady baseline 100 QPS sustained equivalent. Assume we map to 4 GPUs reserved at $3/GPU-hr => $3 * 24 * 30 * 4 = $8640/month (~$8.64k). Add 15% infra ops for private networking & overhead => ~$9936/month (~$10k round).
- If the profile we serve maps to 5k MAUs active under that reserved pool => amortized price = $10k / 5k = $2.00 per MAU/month (floor to cover reserved infra).
- If fewer MAUs (say 2k), amortized = $10k/2k = $5.00 per MAU/month — this is why we want minimum commit sizes or hybrid burst buckets.

SLO / latency premium heuristics:
- Baseline SLO (best-effort / shared hosted): included in PAYG floor.
- 99.9% availability + <150ms p95 interactive latency (dedicated routing + guaranteed capacity): +15–25% premium over reserved baseline.
- 99.95% / <100ms p95 (edge routing, hot-sharding, priority preemption): +30–50% premium.
- If customer requires hard tail guarantees with cold-start elim (prewarmed replicas per tenant): add fixed per-tenant overhead (example: $150–$500/month depending on replica count and model size).

Example bundle quotes (rounded):
- Small startup (hosted PAYG interactive product): $2 / MAU/month (billed PAYG with volume stairs).
- Mid customer (commits to $10k/month reserved, 5k MAUs): amortized $2/MAU + SLO premium 20% => $2.40/MAU/mo.
- Enterprise (lowish MAUs 2k + strict SLO): amortized $5/MAU + SLO premium 30% + per-tenant prewarm $300 => effective ~$6.5/MAU + $300/month fixed.

Other factors to account for (notes):
- Embeddings heavy apps: embedding compute per call and storage cost changes the math; embedding calls often lower token counts but higher model sizes — need separate bucket.
- Cold cache fill (prefix KV/long context): first few requests per session expensive; can amortize across sessions with sticky routing and caching credits.
- Burst behavior: allow burst credits (meter as separate bucket) or price bursts at 2–3x baseline per-token cost.
- Multi-model routing: if we fall back to smaller models for degraded capacity, need transparent discounting or SLA-defined fallback behavior.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Is $3/GPU-hr a defensible internal amortized baseline for hosted (we need infra finance to confirm)?
- How to price function-calling/structured outputs when token counts are low but compute per token remains similar?
- What commit sizes (min $/month) do we want for Dedicated to keep amortization sane?

Quick reference numbers (for copy/paste into quotes):
- Host PAYG floor (this persona): ~$1.83 / MAU/month
- Reserved amortization (example): $10k pool / 5k MAU => $2.00 / MAU/month
- SLO premium guide: 99.9% => +20%, 99.95% => +40%

Notes to self for follow-up:
- Validate GPU/hr input with infra finance; re-run calcs with $/hr sensitivity (2x and 0.5x).
- Build small spreadsheet to swap tokens per request, requests per MAU, model mix.
- Add an embedding-heavy tab (calls per MAU, avg dims, storage + index cost).

End of quick notes. Keep terse; push a cleaned version into PRICING-OVERVIEW once we validate infra rates.
simple_calcs: with ops (x1.3) = $1.4625; price floor with 20% margin = $1.4625 / 0.8 = $1.828
